system.summary: Kerlérec's two-part numerical nomenclator of 1755-62 (about 700 code numbers for letters, syllables, words and names; nine letters with two homophones, usually written stacked).

diacritics.note: No codes for accents or capitals; stacked homophone pairs written one above the other.

prior_solution.where: Pusch 2008 (Louisiana History 49:463-480) rebuilt the code book (547 of 700 entries, Table 2) and says the three despatches, for which no period plaintext is extant, could be decoded with it (p. 468 and n. 13); he summarises the content of no. 206 (pp. 474-475) and no. 207 (p. 475) and shows the first coded lines of no. 215 as an image (p. 465); he prints no French text.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.
tools: Python alignment, decoding and test scripts (scripts/)

solution.what: ANOM C13A 41 and 42 viewed through IIIF crops in Chrome (curl blocked by a proof-of-work page and a 403; not bypassed).
Transcribed 492 code groups of the ministry-deciphered nos. 194 (1759) and 228 (1760, f. 48r) with the clerk's interlinear plaintext and aligned them into 452 group pairs, 164 codes.
Compared the manuscript pairs with Pusch 2008 Table 2: 156 codes agree, 5 spelling variants, 2 differ, 1 not in Pusch.

Froze keys (sha256), wrote a held-out test, then transcribed no. 228 ff. 48v-49r: merged key 243/253 = 96.0% of held-out groups decode to the clerk's word (200 shuffled keys max 17.8%); key from the clerks' glosses (segmented with Pusch's table, so not independent of it) 198/253 = 78.3% (shuffles max 24.1%).
Transcribed nos. 206, 207 (coded passage) and 215 twice, the second pass from the last line upward; one disagreement in 1,068 groups, settled on the image.
Decoded with the clerk's pairs plus Pusch's values where no pair exists: 1,065 of 1,068 legible groups; three codes in no. 206 have no value anywhere.

Paged C13A 41 (1,010 images) and C13A 42 (638 images) at thumbnail crops for further cipher pages and duplicate copies: none of nos. 206, 207, 215; C13A 42 ff. 42-47 is the first copy of no. 228, already deciphered in its second copy.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1065 tokens, 247 types, fr-modern order 4: reading -1.976 per letter; random keys -3.377 (z 11.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.3 (mean -2.322, z 18.3); annealer on the real text -2.283. Verdict: pass.

Integration check of PR #586 (round 13). Counts reproduced by an own parser: 555, 191 and 322 legible groups (1,068), 3 without a value (107, 209, 591), 220 on Pusch's values alone (101, 56, 63), 27 gutter marks. decode.py with the union of key_manuscript.tsv and pusch_values_used.tsv resolves 552/555, 191/191, 322/322. Held-out test re-run: key from the clerks' glosses 198/253 = 78.3% (shuffles mean 16.4%, max 24.1%), identical; test plan and frozen key hashes match. The merged-key figure of 96.0% could not be re-run, the frozen merged key is not in the folder; the union of the two committed key files gives 232/253 = 91.7% (50 shuffles, max 20.2%). Strict word count over the coded text only: 206 278/295 (94.2%), 207 100/103 (97.1%), 215 179/187 (95.7%). ANOM images not sampled: the viewer answered with a bot check and no browser route was available in this session.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: transcriptions, key tied to manuscript pairs, held-out test, first full text of the three despatches. Reading with a known key, not an independent solution.
Anonymous clerks of the Ministry of the Marine: interlinear decipherments of nos. 194 and 228, the source of every manuscript pair.

Donald E. Pusch, 'Kerlérec's Cipher', Louisiana History 49 (2008) 463-480: rebuilt the code book (Table 2), says these three despatches could be decoded with it and summarises nos. 206 and 207 (pp. 474-475); his table was used to segment the clerks' glosses, and 124 of his values are used for codes with no clerk's pair (key/pusch_values_used.tsv).

texts.label: Coded body of no. 206, 3 July 1759 (clear opening and close outside the code)
texts.summary: Kerlérec denounces the cabal of the ordonnateur Rochemore and his officer allies, asks for a frigate and Swiss troops to send them to France, and warns that Indian trade goods have run out.

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling's own AI agents (the working agent; not a person)
reading_review.note: Normalised French read against the English and the raw decode; doubtful groups rechecked on the image. A second AI agent of ours, not shown the readings, confirmed 30 of 30 key pairs and 42 of 42 sampled groups on the captures and reran the test; its corrections are applied. Not an outside check.

gaps.item: Groups lost in the binding gutter at line ends of ff. 81v, 97v and 111v (at least 18, 2 and 7)
gaps.detail: No duplicate copy in C13A 41 or 42; the Library of Congress LCRP microfilm (reel 48) or the leaf itself would restore them.

gaps.item: Codes 107, 209 and 591 in no. 206 have no value in our pairs or in Pusch's table
gaps.detail: Context suggests surpris, ô(ter) and retour/bord (readings/DOUBTS.md); marked as holes.

outcome.method_basis: Key from the Marine clerks' interlinear decipherments of nos. 194 and 228, completed from Pusch 2008 Table 2; three bare despatches decoded with it.

parts.label: Manuscript key
parts.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
parts.basis: 452 group pairs (164 codes) from the clerks' decipherments of nos. 194 and 228, cut into per-code pieces with Pusch's table as the aligner's dictionary.

parts.label: Text of nos. 206, 207, 215
parts.basis: Clerks' values for about 80% of the groups, Pusch 2008 values alone for 220 of 1,068; gutter losses and three unknown codes.

outcome.notes: Lead 1207. First full text and translation of three Kerlérec cipher despatches of 1759 that carry no period decipherment; Pusch 2008 summarised the content of nos. 206 and 207 but printed no text. About a fifth of the groups (220 of 1,068) rest on Pusch's values alone.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.976; polyphony 0.0; 3 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.283

outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration check, 14 Nov 2026, strict count over the coded text of reading_fr_206/207/215.txt: 557 of 585 words (206: 278/295, 207: 100/103, 215: 179/187); a word in brackets, a word with a restored part and a word restored over an encoding slip (readings/DOUBTS.md) are holes; clear lines not counted. The contributor's count, measure_reading.py, is 717 of 744 words with the clear lines included.
